precepts.text: Jeshurun waxed fat and kicked, forsaking the Most High and provoking Him with strange gods and vanities.
precepts.point: All of it comes for the sins of Baasha and Elah, who provoked the Most High to anger with their vanities.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
Moses foretold it: “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”. Israel grew fat, “then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” They “sacrificed unto devils, not to God”, to new gods their fathers never feared.

The Most High says, “they have provoked me to anger with their vanities”. That is the same word spoken over Baasha and Elah his son: all the house of Baasha was destroyed “For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son”, who made Israel to sin, “in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.”

So when Zimri, captain of half his chariots, slew Elah while he was drinking himself drunk in Tirzah, and then left not one male of the house of Baasha, it came “according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet”. It was the Most High answering the provoking of his people.

precepts.text: Solomon's wives turned his heart after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians.
precepts.point: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
Ahab followed the same road Solomon went down: “when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods”, and “Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians”.

Ahab took to wife “Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.” The Zidonians again. Solomon’s heart was turned by his wives, and Ahab’s was turned by his, until he reared up an altar for Baal and made a grove, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger more than all the kings of Israel before him.

precepts.text: Israel is not to marry outside the people, lest their hearts be turned to other gods.
precepts.point: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
The law forbids it: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Israel is not to marry outside the people, lest their hearts be turned to other gods.

Ahab broke that law, and it did exactly what the law warned. As if walking in the sins of Jeroboam were a light thing, he married Jezebel, the daughter of the king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal. Solomon’s wives turned his heart after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Zidonians; Jezebel turned Ahab’s heart to Baal.

precepts.text: Joshua's curse: whoever rebuilds Jericho lays its foundation in his firstborn and sets its gates in his youngest son.
precepts.point: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

precepts.why:
When Jericho fell, Joshua laid a curse on it: “Cursed be the man before the Lord, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.”

In Ahab’s days it came to pass word for word. Hiel the Beth–elite built Jericho, and “laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.” The word of the Most High by Joshua stood, generations later.

precepts.text: When Zimri reigned he slew all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male among his kinsfolk or friends.
precepts.point: The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
This is how the judgment on Baasha was carried out: “when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.” When Zimri reigned, not one male was left.

So when the Most High tells Ahab, “And will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah”, it is plain what that means. The house of Baasha was wiped out to the last male, and the same was coming on Ahab’s house for the provocation wherewith he provoked the Most High and made Israel to sin.

points: The word of the Most High comes to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, because though he was exalted out of the dust and made prince over Israel, he walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin.
